SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / C. B. S. R. L. Station / No. S. D. D. 2588/31 / Date July 22, 1931 / at 23 - 2 - 31）

Subject (in full) Anti-Japanese movement resulting from the Wanpaosan Incident

Made by D. I. Sih Tse-liang. Forwarded by Henry Robertson c.p.i.

As soon as the news of the conflict between the Chinese peasants and the Koreans over the question of farming rights in certain areas of the Vanpaosan District, Kirin, on July 2, 1931, reached Shanghai, the anti-Japanese feeling, which appeared to have subsided since the Anti-Japanese agitation in 1928 - 1929, resulting from the despatch of troops by the Japanese Government to Shantung in April, 1928 and the subsequent collision with the Nationalist troops at Tsinan on May 3, 1928, revived among the local Chinese community. The subsequent reports of incidents which took place in various localities in Korea, in which a number of Chinese immigrants there lost their lives at the hands of the Koreans no doubt intensified the rage of the Chinese people, and the numerous reports received in Shanghai alleging that Japanese policemen, disguised as Koreans were responsible for the outbreak of the recent tragedies naturally directed the hatred and hostility of the Chinese towards the Japanese instead of the Koreans. The Anti-Japanese movement, which was first resuscitated on July 7 during a meeting held by members of the 1st District Kuomintang Headquarters, developed in a series of meeting of Kuomintang members and local labour unions which followed, and reached a climax on July 13, 1931, when about 250 representatives of various local organizations and public bodies held a general meeting in the local Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Honan Road. A special committee entitled "Shanghai Municipality Anti-Japanese and Chinese Emigrants Support Committee" was organized and the following 37 members were elected to serve on the Executive Committee of this organization with the approval of the local Kuomintang Headquarters:

上海公共租界工部局警务处
报告

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 / C. B. S. R. L. 巡捕房 / 编号 S. D. D. 2588/31 / 日期 1931年7月22日 / 于 23 - 2 - 31）

主题（全称） 万宝山事件引发的反日运动

呈报人：特别探员 Sih Tse-liang。转呈人：Henry Robertson，首席巡长。

1931年7月2日，吉林万宝山地区中国农民与朝鲜人之间因耕种权问题发生冲突的消息传至上海后，当地华人社群中自1928-1929年反日 agitation（煽动/运动）以来似乎已平息的反日情绪再度复活；该次运动系因日本政府于1928年4月向山东派兵，以及随后于1928年5月3日在济南与国民党军队发生碰撞所致。此后，关于在朝鲜各地发生的事件的报道，其中许多在朝中国移民死于朝鲜人之手，无疑加剧了中国人民的愤怒；而在上海收到的大量指控称，伪装成朝鲜人的日本警察是近期悲剧爆发的罪魁祸首，这自然将中国人的仇恨和敌意引向了日本人而非朝鲜人。反日运动最初于7月7日在第一区国民党党部成员举行的会议上重新兴起，随后在一系列国民党成员和当地工会举行的会议中得到发展，并于1931年7月13日达到高潮，当时约250名各地方组织和公共团体的代表在北河南路的中国总商会举行了一次全体会议。一个名为“上海市抗日援侨委员会”的特别委员会得以组建，并经当地国民党党部批准，选举以下37名成员担任该组织执行委员会委员：
